# Surly: The Surl and Curl Cookbook

*Preview, 2026-11-21. Stewart Rogers. Oh Really Media.*

A cookbook of network protocol recipes in which every example is a test that runs: a surl that listens, a curl that talks to it, and the result printed beside the claim. Every claim is checked against the current builds of the open-source programs it describes, and the book is built to be read by people and by machines.

## What it is

Every recipe puts a `surl` that listens face to face with a `curl` that talks to it, as two commands, as a C# program, or as an AI agent driving both. [Surl](https://github.com/StewartScottRogers/Surl) is the server-side mate of curl, built to answer every scheme curl can request; [Curl](https://github.com/StewartScottRogers/Curl) is a drop-in replacement for the curl command-line tool. Both are open source, both written in C# on .NET 10 as a matched pair, so each recipe shows a protocol conversation from both ends.

- **Recipes that run.** A recipe is an executable specification. Every claim the text makes is a test case run against the two programs, and the book prints the result beside the claim.
- **Simple to hard.** Ordered by difficulty, not by protocol. Open at any page; each recipe stands alone.
- **Readable by machines.** An index of every recipe by key, problem, protocol, option and exit code; the recipes' test specifications can also serve as a conformance suite for other implementations.

## How it is written

Written and checked with AI agents following a published method: every recipe passes three checks (shape, truth, review), and the author decides what is published. Every decision and its reasons are in the repository.
